chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from al-Minqarī, from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning the saying:
of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed.”
He عليه السلام said: “It does not mean the most deeds, but rather the most correct of you in deed. Correctness is only the fear of Allah, and truthful and good intention.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “Preserving the deed until it becomes pure is harder than the deed itself. The sincere deed is that for which you do not want anyone to praise you except Allah, Mighty and Majestic. And the intention is better than the deed. Indeed, intention is the deed.”
Then he عليه السلام recited His saying, Mighty and Majestic: “Say: Each acts according to his manner” — meaning, according to his intention.

key_terms.أَحْسَنُ عَمَلًا: the best deed; meaning the most correct and sincere action, not merely the most numerous
key_terms.النِّيَّةُ الصَّادِقَةُ: truthful intention directed sincerely for Allah
key_terms.الْعَمَلُ الْخَالِصُ: the deed purified from seeking praise from people
key_terms.خَشْيَةُ اللَّهِ: reverent fear of Allah that guides and purifies deeds
key_terms.شَاكِلَتِهِ: one’s manner or inner disposition, explained here as intention

ai.seo_question: Does Allah value more deeds or more sincere and correct deeds?
ai.summary: This narration explains that the divine test is not about the quantity of deeds, but their soundness and sincerity. Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام teaches that true correctness in action rests on khashyah of Allah and truthful intention, and that guarding a deed from corruption by showing off is harder than merely doing it. The passage also links outward action to inward intention through the Quranic statement that each person acts according to his disposition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Qasim Bin Muhammad, from Al Minqary, from Sufyan Bin Uyayna, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Words of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic [67:2] that He may Test you - which of you is best in deeds.

He<sup>asws</sup> said ‘It does not Mean the abundance of deeds, but the correct ones of your deeds, and rather the correctness is the fear of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the truthful intention, and the good deeds’.

Then he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘The remaining upon the deed until it finishes is more difficult than performing the deed itself, and the sincere deed is that which you do not want to be praised upon by anyone except for Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic; and the intention is superior than the deed itself. Indeed! The intention, it is the deed’.
Then heasws recited the Words of the Mighty and Majestic [17:84] Say: Every one acts according to his own disposition – Meaning, upon his intention’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad from al-Minqari from Sufyan ibn ‘Uyayna from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “About the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘So that He may try you to see who among you is best in good deeds. . . .’ [67:2], the Imam said, ‘He has not meant thereby the quantity of deeds. He thereby has meant the most correct ones in deeds. Correctness comes only from overwhelming respect for Allah, true intention and goodness.’

He then said, ‘It comes from continuity of the good deeds. In fact, maintaining continuity until deeds reach purity is more difficult than performing the deed itself. It is the intention that forms the deed.’
The Imam then recited the words of Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, ‘Say (O Muhammad), “Everyone acts according to his way,” [17:84] it (way) means according to his intentions.’”
